title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes study, for each 'lieu' L (a tame/stratified space), a lattice F_L = Figures(L) of figures or multistructures. This lattice has a meet written X.Y, a unit element 1 (the total support), complements, and relations ≤, ≪, ⊂° (interior inclusion) and |∘| (interiors meet). The previous page treated an inclusion i : L_0 ↪ L. There i_* : Fig(L_0) → Fig(L) is fully faithful with image Fig(L)_{L_0}. Restriction Fig(L) → Fig(L_0) is presented as a 'passage to the quotient' that formally sets X = ∅ whenever X°∩L_0 = ∅.

This page compares i_* with the inverse image f^*. Both are 'plongements' in some sense, but there is an important difference. In all cases considered (F_L, F_{L'}, F_{L_0}) there is a greatest element. For f^*, and for maps of the immersion kind, the unit (total support) goes to the unit. For i_* (an immersion towards an inclusion) it does not: i_*(1) is the support of L_0, not of L. Restated for supports:
- φ^* preserves the total support and commutes with complementation.
- φ_* does neither.

For an inclusion φ = i : L_0 ↪ L he records three identities:
- i^* i_* = id_{F_0};
- i_* i^*(X) = i_*(1).X;
- more generally the 'projection formula' i_*(X').Y = i_*(X'.i^*(Y)).

These are the lattice versions of i^{-1}(i(A)) = A, i(i^{-1}B) = i(L_0)∩B, and f(A∩f^{-1}B) = f(A)∩B.

Finally, on preservation of sups and infs:
- Both φ^* and φ_* commute with arbitrary Sups, including φ^*(∅) = ∅.
- φ_* commutes with Infs of non-empty families, since the empty Inf 1 is not preserved.

The upshot is that i_* identifies F_{L_0} with the interval [0, i_*(1)] of F_L, while i^* is the retraction X ↦ X.i_*(1). The next page uses this to warn that f^* for non-surjective f involves a quotient: it preserves ≪° and |∘| but not ≤ or ≪, since Y' = ∅ is possible with X' ≠ ∅. Such maps therefore must be handled carefully in defining morphisms of 'ateliers'.
errors: Commutation of φ_* with non-empty Infs holds only for injective φ (inclusions/immersions); for a general map, images do not commute with intersections. Read in context (φ = i an inclusion) the claim is correct, but the sentence is phrased for φ_* in general.
'Sups quelconques': in lattices of tame figures (e.g. semi-algebraic/stratified sets) only finite sups exist in general, so 'quelconques' should be read as 'those that exist' or 'finite'.

The sentence on which maps send the unit to the unit is garbled. Mathematically: φ^* always preserves 1, φ_* = i_* preserves 1 only if i is surjective. The contrast is stated correctly a few lines later.

ideas.what: Projection formula i_*(X').Y = i_*(X'.i^*Y) for direct/inverse image of figures under an inclusion
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius reciprocity / projection formula for ∃_f ⊣ f^* on subobject lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lawvere (hyperdoctrines, 1969); projection formula in sheaf theory (Grothendieck/SGA4, Verdier)
ideas.where_published: Projection formulas in SGA4/SGA5 (sheaf/cohomological setting); not in this lattice-of-figures form

ideas.what: i^* i_* = id and i_* i^*(X) = i_*(1).X: an inclusion identifies the figure lattice of L_0 with the interval below i_*(1)
ideas.modern_name: Embedding of a lattice as a principal down-set; retraction by meet

ideas.what: Contrast: f^* preserves top, complements, sups and infs (a Boolean homomorphism); f_* preserves sups and, for injective f, non-empty infs but not top or complement
ideas.modern_name: Inverse image as Boolean algebra morphism vs. direct image as left adjoint

ideas.what: Viewing restriction to L_0 as a quotient of Fig(L) by an ideal of 'negligible' figures (continued from the previous page)
ideas.modern_name: Quotient of a lattice/Boolean algebra by an ideal; localization

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary lattice-theoretic properties of direct and inverse image (projection formula, preservation of sups/infs/complements) for inclusions, in Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology framework. Context of minor historical interest, but no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top is '48', and the neighbours are probably 47 and 49 (transcribed as '17' and '89').
'il y a une plus grande[?] dimension[?] F_L, F_{L'}, F_{L_0}' should probably read 'il y a un plus grand élément' (the unit 1) in each of F_L, F_{L'}, F_{L_0}.
'Dans φ* de nos supports' likely reads 'Dans le cas de nos supports'.
The formula should read i_* i^*(X) = i_*(1).X, written with corrections in the manuscript.
Last line: 'et φ_* aux Inf^s de familles non vides' — φ^* commutes with all Infs, while φ_* (inclusion) commutes only with non-empty ones.
